title: What is known about 1RB1LD_1RC1RE_1LA0RA_1RC0LB_0LA1RF_---1RB
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LD_1RC1RE_1LA0RA_1RC0LB_0LA1RF_---1RB.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: Open. The tape is a list of registers, runs of the word 011101 with short separators. The first register grows while the second shrinks, about four units for one, and when the second runs low the list shifts by one. The transfer and shift rules have not been extracted. Direct simulation: no halt in 1011 steps.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 59,855 cells have been visited and 47,179 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.494). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.075).

claims.title: The register rules
claims.text: The transfer between the first two registers and the shift; see the README's For later.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB0LB_1LC1RE_1LA1LD_0RB1LF_1LA0RC_---1LC up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: Units gained by the first register per unit lost by the second (observed).

sections.heading: Registers of 011101
html:
Read left to right, the tape is a list of registers: runs of the word 011101 separated by short separators. Their lengths at the left end at a few moments (separators left out):

step 12,547,595:   670   87  144   21
step 14,175,202:   136  652   75  140   21
step 53,840,380:    11 1019  509  430   19  127   17
step 99,822,398:  1370  680  425  409   12  124   15

The first register grows while the second shrinks, about four units for one; when the second runs low the list shifts (the old first register becomes the second, a new first register starts small). The width grows like the square root of the step count. The units are crossed by shift rules (A moving right turns 011101 into 111110, D moving left turns it into 111011).

sections.heading: Not known
html: The machine halts only in F reading 0 (E reads a 1 and moves right onto a 0). The registers look like a cascade of counters, but the transfer and shift rules have not been extracted, so there is no map to iterate. Direct simulation: no halt in 1011 steps.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.494). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.075).
After 109 steps the tape spans 59,855 cells (40,774 left of the start, 50 right), with a density of 1s of 0.788.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machine below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in the other, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

  • 1RB0LB_1LC1RE_1LA1LD_0RB1LF_1LA0RC_---1LC: rename A→B, B→C, C→A, D→E, E→D, F→F and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state C, in a mirror

summary: A cascade of registers made of the word 011101: the first grows about four units for each unit the second loses, then the list shifts; no halt in 10^11 steps; the rules are not decoded.
